channel.title: Stellar Property Management — Association Board Guides
channel.description: Illinois condominium, HOA, and townhome association guidance for Chicago and North Shore boards, from a licensed community association management firm.

item.title: Resale Disclosure Fees and Deadlines in Illinois: Condo vs. HOA
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Illinois condo 22.1 disclosures: 10 business days, fee capped at $375 adjusted by CPI, $100 rush within 72 hours. HOAs under CICAA 1-35: 30 days and a reasonable cost-based fee.

item.title: What a Chicago Condo Management Transition Looks Like: The First 60 Days
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: What Illinois condo and HOA boards should expect in the first 60 days after they hire a new manager: records, funds, vendors, notices and a clean handoff.

item.title: Financial-Only vs Full-Service Condo and HOA Management in Chicago
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: A Chicago board guide to financial-only versus full-service association management: what each includes, how to compare proposals, and when a fuller scope is a better fit.

item.title: Running a Glenview Townhome or HOA Board: A Local Guide
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: A guide for Glenview townhome, HOA and condo boards: master and sub-associations at The Glen, aging townhome roofs and roads, snow contracts, and which Illinois law applies.

item.title: Does a Small Condo Association Need a Professional Manager?
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: An honest look at when a small Chicago condo association (6 to 30 units) can self-manage, when it should hire a manager, and what professional management actually changes.

item.title: No Heat in a Chicago Condo Building: A Board Protocol
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: What Chicago’s Heat Ordinance requires (68°F day, 66°F night, Sept. 15 to June 1), and a step-by-step protocol for condo boards when central heat or hot water fails.

item.title: High-Rise Condo Management in Chicago: What Is Different
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Why a Chicago high-rise condominium needs a different kind of management than a walk-up: staff, building systems, City inspection programs, capital planning and 24/7 response.

item.title: Smoke and CO Alarms in Illinois Condo Buildings
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Illinois law requires alarms within 15 feet of every sleeping room and a smoke detector at the top of every interior stairwell. Who installs and maintains them in a condominium.

item.title: Snow and Ice: What Illinois Law Actually Protects
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: The Illinois Snow and Ice Removal Act protects residential sidewalk clearing from liability unless willful or wanton. Chicago requires clearing by 10 p.m. or 10 a.m. with a 5-foot path.

item.title: Solar Panels in Illinois Associations: Who Has the Right
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: The Illinois Homeowners’ Energy Policy Statement Act bars associations from prohibiting solar — but not for buildings over 60 feet or with a shared roof. The policy, the deadlines and the limits.

item.title: Flags and Flagpoles: What Illinois Owners May Display
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Illinois law bars condo and HOA boards from prohibiting the American flag, military flags and flagpoles on limited common elements. What boards may still regulate, and what the law omits.

item.title: How Long Must an Illinois Association Keep Its Records?
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Section 19 of the Illinois Condominium Property Act sets retention periods: 7 years of minutes, 10 fiscal years of books and records, 12 months of ballots. The full schedule for boards.

item.title: Six Months of Assessments After an Illinois Foreclosure
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Section 9(g) of the Illinois Condominium Property Act sets what a foreclosure purchaser owes an association: assessments from the month after the sale, plus up to six months of arrears.

item.title: The 115% Rule: When Owners Can Reject an Assessment
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Illinois owners can petition to vote on a budget or special assessment that pushes total assessments above 115% of last year. The 20% petition, the deadlines and the exceptions.

item.title: What Illinois Law Requires Your Condo Master Policy to Cover
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Section 12 of the Illinois Condominium Property Act sets minimum master policy coverage: full insurable replacement cost, demolition and increased cost of construction, and $1,000,000 liability.

item.title: Critical Repairs: What Disqualifies a Condo Building
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Fannie Mae treats a project needing critical repairs as ineligible. The definition, the $10,000-per-unit threshold, the three-year inspection rule, and what boards should fix first.

item.title: Ordering a Reserve Study a Lender Will Accept in 2027
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Fannie Mae will accept a reserve study instead of the reserve percentage test only on strict conditions: three years, no baseline funding, and the highest recommended allocation in the budget.

item.title: Is Our Small HOA Exempt From the Illinois Association Act?
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: CICAA exempts some small Illinois HOAs and townhome associations. The 10-unit, $100,000 and $50,000 thresholds in Section 1-75, and what they mean for the 2027 collection policy.

item.title: Five Collection Policy Decisions Your Board Must Make
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: The new Illinois collection policy law lists what the policy must cover but leaves the hard choices to the board. The five decisions to settle before January 1, 2027.

item.title: Illinois Condo Boards Must Have an Accessible Parking Policy
item.dc:creator: Mirsad Cerimovic, CAM, CMCA, AMS
item.description: Section 18.12 of the Illinois Condominium Property Act requires every condo board to adopt an accessible parking policy with a review period of no more than 45 days. What it must contain.
